_comment: chiSurf-compatible detector_setups.json for the polarization-resolved two-colour MFD instrument that examples/simulation/configs/mfd_2col_2pol.json simulates. Byte-compatible with ~/.chisurf/detector_setups.json: the CLI reads `setups.<name>.detectors.<name>.chs` and ignores everything else chiSurf keeps here. Channel convention follows chiSurf's tttr_channel_definition_tttr_io.py: within a detector chs[::2] is parallel and chs[1::2] is perpendicular, so `green` = [0, 8] is green-parallel on 0 and green-perpendicular on 8 -- which is what the simulation emits (its channel order is green-par, green-perp, red-par, red-perp, mapped onto routing 0, 8, 1, 9), and getting it backwards inverts every anisotropy computed from the file without changing a single photon count. The four-detector setup below names each arm separately, which is what makes the burst table carry per-polarization columns.
